newsitem.title: FINLAND: Restructuring boosts Asko to 34-mth highs.
newsitem.headline: Restructuring boosts Asko to 34-mth highs.

text.p: Shares in Finnish plastic pipes, white goods and furniture maker Asko Oy rose in heavy trading on Wednesday sparked by demand due to the company's ongoing streamlining process, brokers said.
At 1225/1025 GMT, Asko traded at 310 markka, up seven markka or 2.31 percent, its highest since February 1994.
Turnover was heavy for Asko at 52 million markka -- 44 million markka in a singe large in-house deal by Evli at 305 markka. Evli declined to comment on the deal.
"The interest in Asko has to do with the restructuring in the company," one broker said.
"It has divested operations in order to focus on its core businesses," he added.

Asko recently annouced plans to sell its cross-country skiing and footwear businesses which are part of its Karhu Sport Oy unit. On Novemeber 6, Asko said it had signed a letter of intent to sell its Forssan Saha saw mill.
No one at the company was available for comment.
